wineries.name: Edwards Wines
wineries.specialty: Estate wines named for the founder's Tiger Moth, with an Oceans Series aged beneath Flinders Bay
wineries.description: The estate a biplane built: founded by an aviator whose 1943 Tiger Moth hangs in the cellar door, and whose wines age eighteen metres under the sea at Augusta.
wineries.story: In 1990 Brian Edwards flew his 1943 Tiger Moth, Matilda, solo from England to Australia in one of the epic charity flights of modern aviation. The journey ended in Perth, and a year later Brian and his wife Jenny bought this Margaret River property for its gravel loams, its water, and the fact that Brian could fit an airstrip out the back. Son Christo planted the first Semillon in 1993, eldest son Michael made the first wine in 1999, and today Matilda herself holds pride of place inside the cellar door, lending her name to the core range. The estate's Oceans Series goes further still: bottles are sealed, crated and lowered eighteen metres into the ocean at Flinders Bay, Augusta, where the sea's steady temperature and pressure act as a natural cellar.

image.alt: Aerial view over the Edwards vineyard, dam and red-dirt track at golden hour
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: aerial of estate vineyard with dam and red gravel track

briefing.icebreaker: The aeroplane above the tasting bench is Matilda, the 1943 Tiger Moth the founder flew solo from England to Australia in 1990; the Matilda wines are named after her.
briefing.proMove: Tastings are complimentary and walk-ins welcome; ask about the Oceans Series, aged eighteen metres beneath Flinders Bay at Augusta, and how the same wine tastes different after a year under the sea.
briefing.hiddenGem: Brian chose this block partly because he could fit an airstrip behind the vines, and the family's aviation obsession is everywhere once you start looking.

wineries.sommNote: The only cellar door in the valley with a trans-continental biplane over the bar and a cellar under the ocean; the wines live up to the stories.

wineries.name: Ashbrook Estate
wineries.specialty: Single-vineyard Semillon, Verdelho and Chardonnay from one of Wilyabrup's 1970s pioneers
wineries.description: A no-fuss 1975 pioneer on Tom Cullity Drive that has quietly logged more than forty consecutive estate vintages, still family owned and operated.
wineries.story: The Devitt family planted Ashbrook in 1975 among the forest off what is now Tom Cullity Drive, and by 2022 the estate was marking its 44th consecutive vintage as a family-owned, single-vineyard producer. While neighbours built restaurants and galleries, Ashbrook kept its head down and its prices honest, earning a devoted following for its whites, especially a Verdelho regarded among Australia's best.

image.alt: Autumn-gold vine rows at Ashbrook Estate with forest behind
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: autumn vineyard rows against forest, no people

briefing.icebreaker: Ashbrook has notched more than forty consecutive estate vintages under one family, a Wilyabrup record few neighbours can match.
briefing.proMove: Ask for the Verdelho: it is one of the few serious examples in Australia and rarely leaves the cellar door.
briefing.hiddenGem: The estate sits on Tom Cullity Drive within a short hop of Vasse Felix, Juniper and Thompson, making it the sleeper stop on the region's most storied road.

wineries.sommNote: The connoisseur's detour: nowhere else in the valley does Verdelho this seriously, and the Semillon is built like the Hunter's best.

wineries.visitorSummary: Reviewers regularly find a founding family member behind the bar: history-first tastings, big flavours from a small outfit, and the Riesling a repeated surprise favourite.

wineries.name: Fraser Gallop Estate
wineries.specialty: Dry-grown Parterre and Palladian Chardonnay and Cabernet from a Halliday five-star estate
wineries.description: A meticulously groomed Metricup Road estate whose dry-grown Chardonnay and Cabernet have collected international trophies at a startling rate.
wineries.story: Nigel Gallop planted this Metricup Road vineyard in 1999 and set about making wines with Old World restraint from dry-grown Wilyabrup fruit. The gamble paid off quickly: James Halliday rates the estate five stars, the Parterre Chardonnay was ranked number two in WA at the 2025 WA Good Food Guide awards, and the wines now feature in The Wine Advocate's Australian new-release coverage. The manicured grounds, complete with the Georgian-style Gallop House across the lake, are worth the drive alone.

image.alt: Aerial view of Gallop House across the lake and vine rows at Fraser Gallop Estate
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: aerial of Georgian-style Gallop House, lake and vineyard

briefing.icebreaker: The vines here are dry-grown, no irrigation at all, which is rare even by Wilyabrup's spoilt standards.
briefing.proMove: Taste the Parterre Chardonnay against the flagship Palladian if it is open; the step up in tension is a masterclass in what oak restraint buys.
briefing.hiddenGem: Gallop House, the Georgian-style homestead across the lake, hosts long lunches and stays; even from the cellar door it is the region's most photogenic folly.

wineries.sommNote: Wilyabrup's quiet perfectionist: dry-grown fruit, surgical winemaking, and a Chardonnay pair that embarrasses far dearer bottles.
wineries.visitorSummary: Personalised estate tours and warm hosting are the theme, and the double brie on the cheeseboard has its own fan club.

wineries.name: McHenry Hohnen
wineries.specialty: Certified biodynamic single-vineyard Chardonnay and alternative varieties from Hazel's and Calgardup Brook
wineries.description: The biodynamic single-vineyard project of Cape Mentelle founder David Hohnen, poured at a slick Vintners Wine Bar on the Witchcliffe corner.
wineries.story: David Hohnen, the man who founded Cape Mentelle and Cloudy Bay, teamed up with his brother-in-law Murray McHenry in 2004 to make wines purely from their family vineyards in the region's south. Everything is certified biodynamic, farmed with minimal intervention and bottled by single site, from the taut Calgardup Brook Chardonnay to Australia's most convincing Zinfandel off Hazel's Vineyard. The cellar door doubles as the Vintners Wine Bar, all circular marri bar and bottle halo.

image.alt: The circular bar and hanging bottle rack of the Vintners Wine Bar at McHenry Hohnen
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-11, viewed and verified: interior of Vintners Wine Bar, circular bar with bottle halo

briefing.icebreaker: The founder made Cloudy Bay famous before coming home to farm biodynamically; ask what he thinks of Sauvignon Blanc these days.
briefing.proMove: Walk-ins are fine for the standard tasting, but the single-vineyard flight is the point: Calgardup Brook against Burnside shows two Chardonnays a few kilometres and a world apart.
briefing.hiddenGem: Hazel's Vineyard grows Zinfandel, Tempranillo and Grenache alongside the classics; the Zin is the most serious example in the country.

wineries.sommNote: Where Margaret River goes when it wants to argue about terroir: one family, certified biodynamic, and every bottle traceable to a single paddock.

wines.name: Reserve Chardonnay
wines.description: The estate flagship white: ripe lemon and lime, white nectarine and a flinty mineral line off the family's oldest Chardonnay rows.
wines.sommNote: Serve at 11C rather than fridge-cold; the flint needs a little warmth to speak.

wines.name: Matilda Cabernet Malbec
wines.description: From the range named for the founder's Tiger Moth: cassis, dark chocolate and red earth in an honest, early-drinking frame.
wines.sommNote: The label honours a biplane, not a person; drink it with the story and a barbecue.

wines.name: Shiraz Grenache Rosé
wines.description: Salmon-pink and lifted, all cranberry, musk and citrus with a delicate dry finish.
wines.sommNote: Made for the esky and the Gracetown lookout; drink it young and cold.

wines.name: Semillon
wines.description: A single-vineyard Semillon in the taut, age-worthy idiom, picked early and bottled without fuss.
wines.sommNote: Buy two: one for tonight's fish, one for the back of the cellar where it will do a Hunter-style transformation.

wines.name: Verdelho
wines.description: One of Australia's few serious Verdelhos: tropical fruit with a fresh citrus spine, off vines planted by the founding Devitts.
wines.sommNote: The cellar-door cult buy; it rarely reaches shops, so take a case while you can.

wines.name: Cabernet Merlot
wines.description: A classically built Wilyabrup blend, all leaf and cassis, from one of the valley's longest continuously farmed single vineyards.
wines.sommNote: Forty-plus consecutive vintages of practice show in the tannin polish; decant thirty minutes.

wines.name: Parterre Chardonnay
wines.description: Ranked second in WA at the 2025 WA Good Food Guide awards: dry-grown Wilyabrup Chardonnay wound tight around a mineral core.
wines.sommNote: Give it ten minutes out of the ice; the struck-match note blossoms into white peach and nougat.

wines.name: Palladian Chardonnay
wines.description: The estate icon, made in tiny quantities with Old World restraint; among the most decorated Chardonnays in the state.
wines.sommNote: Cellar-worthy and severe in youth; if you open it now, decant it like a red and serve at 12C.

wines.name: Parterre Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: Dry-grown Wilyabrup Cabernet with graphite edges and a long cedar finish, built on the estate's trophy-winning form.
wines.sommNote: Drinks like a Margaux understudy at a fraction of the bill; decant an hour.

wines.name: Calgardup Brook Chardonnay
wines.description: Biodynamic single-vineyard Chardonnay from limestone country near the coast: saline, taut and slow to unwind.
wines.sommNote: The sea-spray salinity is the signature; serve at 11C with anything that swam.

wines.name: Hazel's Vineyard Zinfandel
wines.description: Australia's most convincing Zinfandel, grown biodynamically on Hazel's Vineyard: dark cherry, spice and a savoury tail.
wines.sommNote: Hohnen fell for Zin in California; taste why. Serve just below room temperature with anything char-grilled.

wines.name: Rocky Road Shiraz
wines.description: The estate's everyday red: biodynamic single-vineyard Shiraz at a price that shames the category.
wines.sommNote: The smart weeknight buy of the whole region; a certified biodynamic single-vineyard wine for under thirty dollars.
